scene.intent: Revised selected warm watercolor direction with perpendicular camera, legible 2D platform, integrated reflector and actual tail tip
scene.prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render / stylized-concept. Create a revised first-level art prototype for a poetic 2D side-scrolling knowledge-based puzzle platformer, not a 3D exploration game.
REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 is ONLY the reference for a near-front wall elevation and a continuous horizontal stage strip; do not reproduce its asset-board layout or cold palette. Image 2 is the PRIMARY reference for the warm brick watercolor storybook painting style, lush foliage, tiny glowing spirit identity, materials, and overall garden scale. Recompose it according to the corrections below. One complete scene only, no panels or captions.
CAMERA IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CHANGE: the camera looks straight perpendicular at the long garden wall, horizontal optical axis, no sideways yaw, no downward tilt, orthographic side-view for gameplay. Wall pillars vertical, wall courses horizontal, no converging courtyard or three-quarter stage angle. Show this as a flat 2D game screen, not an isometric diorama. Rear scenic artwork can suggest gentle depth, but the PLAYABLE path is one unmistakable horizontal ledge across the bottom. Landscape wide composition.
GROUND READABILITY: Put the continuous walkable platform lip at roughly 82 percent of canvas height. Its side-facing masonry/earth/roots fill the lower 18 percent, strongly outlined with dark warm charcoal. The lip stays almost horizontal left to right, with just two low side-profile entrance steps at far left and one harmless half-brick step near the lamp. No broad tilted tabletop floor. Only a very thin hint of top surface at the lip. Behind this path, a narrow softer, lower-contrast strip of garden earth recedes to the wall; it reads as scenery, not another walkable lane. All foreground standing feet and object bases belong on the same visible platform route.
COMPOSITION: warm red-brick and pale plaster boundary wall, immense shaded tree canopy over upper third/two-thirds, old front-facing iron garden gate cropped at far left, low planted brick flowerbed at middle left with sparse tiny orange flowers, an exterior wall/doorframe closing the far right. Large quiet vertical wall area. A single small jagged sunlight opening in wall around x=60 percent y=42 percent. Tiny white-gold wick spirit with huge swept flame head and extra small body, two oval eyes, tiny arms/legs, gold chest ember; total height 5 percent of image, stands on the clear foreground lip left of center.
INTEGRATE THE REFLECTOR INTO THE ENVIRONMENT: Completely remove the freestanding mirror/pedestal from Image 2. In its place at x=51 percent, fix the remains of an OLD GARDEN WALL LANTERN to the low front/side edge of the existing brick flowerbed, just behind the playable lip. Its corroded iron bracket is visibly mortared into the flowerbed. Broken lantern hood/frame and missing glass, no working lamp/bulb/flame. A single FLAT SILVERED BACKPLATE is still attached inside it by one VERTICAL iron hinge. This is the actual rotatable reflector, partly swung open like a small hinged door. It is a salvaged integral piece of the lantern, NOT a handheld looking glass, NOT a pedestal mirror, NOT a new machine. A modest exposed bent tab at its lower edge is within the spirit's reach from the low half-brick step. Reflective face bright silver, surrounding iron dull and ivy partly covering the outer bracket. A few dull fallen lantern fragments below explain its origin. Make the lamp and pivot big enough to read, but secondary to the overall garden.
ONE REFLECTION: one delicate warm beam descends LEFTWARD from the wall opening to the silver backplate; one straight thinner reflected beam goes RIGHTWARD and slightly DOWN from that exact point to the tail scale. The change of direction happens ON the mirror face only. Clear unobstructed air between reflector and target, through the open side of the fallen stonework, not through solid walls. Do not add rays, lens flares, extra mirrors, floating glint sources or UI.
REPLACE THE EGG/STONE WITH AN ACTUAL TAIL TIP: At x=77-86 percent, beneath/among a low collapsed stone stair and rubble at right, show only the final short section of the giant light-eating creature's tail. It is a continuous elongated gently curved organic appendage lying horizontally, grey-ivory and pale blue with a few overlapping leaf-shaped scales. Its thicker BASE on the RIGHT disappears under the rubble and continues into unseen darkness; the tapered soft POINT curves slightly LEFT toward the mirror. Exposed length about 12 percent of screen width, thickness 3-4 percent of height. One scale near the tapered tip, flush with the skin, gently glows warm pearl gold where the reflected ray lands. The rest stays quieter, chalky and alive. The silhouette must clearly read as a long tapering tail, NOT an egg, gemstone, round luminous boulder, isolated oval, severed organ, worm animal, face, head, limb or entire creature. Stone blocks partially overlap the thick base; taper and directional scale flow remain visible.
EXIT: an upside-down chipped terracotta flowerpot at far right on the same route, rim on ground, small drainage hole on its upper closed base, a dark little arched broken opening at the bottom rim facing left/front. Enough space for the tiny spirit to enter. Not a pot lying sideways.
STYLE: retain Image 2's sophisticated warm watercolor-and-ink illustrated fairytale quality, paper granulation, honey sunlight, terracotta, muted sage moss and blue-grey shadows, delicate leaf shapes and natural masonry. Foreground lip, low steps, lantern reflector mechanism, tail silhouette and pot entrance use clear dark ink outlines; distant vegetation/wall quieter and softer. Artful and intimate, not photorealistic, not glossy 3D, not cute toy diorama. No text, interface, labels, arrows, diagram marks, white borders, sheet layout, additional creatures or giant-body reveal.

detail.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Make an intimate watercolor GAME PROP DESIGN SHEET, using the attached revised level scene as the exact design reference. Warm ivory paper backdrop, delicate ink drawing and watercolor textures like the reference, generous clear spacing, no decorative borders. Not a game screenshot. Two columns: LEFT is one large close-up of the existing flowerbed-mounted broken garden lantern with its hinged silver reflector; RIGHT is two smaller matched side-profile close-ups of exactly the same beast tail-tip in the same rubble gap, upper unlit, lower first light absorbed.
LEFT: Keep the warm brick flowerbed edge, tiny orange flowers and ivy, old dull corroded iron mounting bracket visibly embedded in masonry, broken lantern cage with missing glass, and its one rectangular FLAT silvered internal backplate hinged at a VERTICAL edge and partly opened like a little door. This reflective plate belongs to the lantern assembly, not an independent floor mirror. Show vertical hinge knuckles clearly. It has fixed mounting tilt and swivels left-right around that upright hinge. A small connected bent iron operating tab descends to near the lower brick ledge, visibly within reach of the tiny light spirit standing on that ledge. The entire spirit is about one lantern-body height: large flame-shaped pale head, tiny body, gold chest. No freestanding pedestal. No electrical wires or modern components. Lantern is unlit, faceplate alone gleams from exterior sunlight; maintain optical open space around it. Keep side-on platform edge horizontal and wall frontal. Only one reflector.
RIGHT TOP and RIGHT BOTTOM: Match each other and the tail in the reference. Each shows a SHORT EXPOSED TAPERING CURVED TAIL SECTION, thick base entering dark rubble on RIGHT, pointed end extending LEFT. It belongs to an enormous hidden animal. Grey-ivory, pale blue overlapping leaf-shaped scales flow in one direction. It lies horizontally and only curves gently; NOT an oval, round stone, egg, disconnected object, claw, face or snake animal. Two or three mossy stone blocks cover its base. In the TOP study, all tail scales are matte chalky grey and the tip rests heavily. In the BOTTOM study, ONE flush scale near the tapered tip softly glows pearl gold with tiny warm veins spreading through adjacent skin; the tip rises a barely visible amount to suggest its first breath, thick base stays buried. A single thin ray from off-frame left ends at this particular scale; do not illuminate every scale or make the tail a gold jewel. The overall silhouette remains the same in both.
Only these three studies, clean attractive production design board. No labels or written text, no arrows, no extra views, no large background scenery, no UI. Clearly drawn, easy to understand material construction, preserve reference art and species identity.

handle_refinement.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Input Image 1 is the edit target: the full side-view garden game scene. Input Image 2 is a supporting construction reference only: the lantern close-up and tail studies. Keep Image 1's entire composition, camera, watercolor rendering, dimensions, character size/location, platform, beam path, tail and pots unchanged.
Make ONE local usability adjustment only, at the existing flowerbed-mounted wall lantern. Make the old bent metal control rod connected to the reflector's upright hinge extend visibly downward along the flowerbed wall. End it in a small rounded horizontal iron grip just ABOVE the little pile of bricks, at about the waist/chest height of the protagonist when it would stand beside the lamp on the same foreground walking ledge. The grip should be visibly reachable with no high jumping: about 30-40 pixels above the ledge in this composition. The hinge-to-handle linkage is narrow, aged, mechanically continuous and attached to the lantern bracket; give the grip a small worn brass highlight to be readable against dark brick. This is a compact salvaged handle belonging to the lantern, not a giant floor switch or new standalone object. Use Image 2's lower-operating-tab idea but match Image 1's scale. Do not change the reflector face, rays, animal tail, platform profile or any other scene element. Do not add UI, lettering, arrows, characters, panels or borders. One complete scene, unchanged apart from a clearly reachable linked control handle.
